idiom_name: OpenStruct / property methods defined per instance (define_singleton_method)
implementation_notes: Ruby realizes the pattern through method lookup: OpenStruct 'utilizes Ruby's method lookup structure to find and define the necessary methods for properties', implemented with method_missing and define_singleton_method, so its @table Hash is the property list and the singleton getters/setters are the dynamic members. Object#instance_variable_set/get plus define_singleton_method give the same per-instance members without a class per property set, and implement respond_to_missing? so respond_to? and duck-typing checks tell the truth. The classic structure is absorbed into the object model; for a fixed attribute set Hash, Struct or Data is faster and checked.
code_sketch:
require "ostruct"

order = OpenStruct.new(id: "A-17")   # @table (a Hash) is the property list
order.routing_slip = "RS-17"        # define_singleton_method adds getter and setter
order.to_h                          # discoverability: key/value pairs
order.delete_field(:routing_slip)   # remove again at run time

class Bag                           # hand-rolled: any name, one class
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    key = name.to_s.chomp("=").to_sym
    @props.key?(key) ? @props[key] : super
  end
  def respond_to_missing?(name, _all = false)   # keep respond_to? honest
    @props.key?(name.to_s.chomp("=").to_sym) || super
  end
end
pitfalls: OpenStruct defines a singleton method per property name, so a new key invalidates method caches: the docs warn that OpenStruct use is discouraged for performance reasons (roughly 200x slower than reading an equivalent Hash) and that building one from untrusted data risks a symbol denial of service, because method names are never garbage collected.
method_missing without respond_to_missing? lies to respond_to?, duck-typing checks and documentation tools; it must also call super for unknown names or real NoMethodError bugs are swallowed.
Per-instance singleton methods and OpenStruct tables do not share cleanly across Ractors and complicate marshalling; for a fixed attribute set prefer Struct/Data or an explicit Hash.

variants.name: Per-instance property methods (define_singleton_method / instance_variable_set)
variants.idiom_name: define_singleton_method + respond_to_missing? over an explicit Hash
variants.implementation_notes: Hand-rolled form: keep the properties in a Hash ivar and define the accessor methods on the object's singleton class per key (define_singleton_method) or answer unmatched names through method_missing, with respond_to_missing? mirroring the key set. It costs one method per property (same cache churn as OpenStruct) but keeps full control over naming, validation and storage, and avoids OpenStruct's table-in-every-instance layout; choose it when some properties must be validated or computed and others stored.
pitfalls: Every dynamically defined method occupies the singleton class for the object's lifetime, so a long-lived object fed user-supplied names exhausts the method table (the same hazard OpenStruct documents).
Singletons are invisible to Marshal and to other Ractors unless the state lives in normal ivars and is wrapped appropriately.
